title: Raspberry crumble bars
summary: Fresh raspberries baked between an almond shortbread base and a cinnamon nut crumble, dairy-free as written.
steps: Heat the oven to 175 °C (350 °F). Line a 20 cm (8 in) square pan with parchment.
Mix the almond flour, coconut flour, erythritol, baking powder and salt. Rub in the coconut oil, then mix in the egg and vanilla to a crumbly dough.
Press two-thirds of the dough into the pan and bake 12 minutes.
Mix the remaining dough with the sliced almonds and cinnamon, pinching it into clumps.
Toss the raspberries with the erythritol, lemon juice and chia seeds and spread over the warm base. Scatter the crumble on top.
Bake 25–30 minutes, until the crumble is golden and the fruit bubbles at the edges.
Cool completely, then chill 1 hour so the filling sets before cutting into 16 squares.
tips: Frozen raspberries work; don't thaw them, and add 5 minutes to the bake.

origin.history: The fruit crumble became popular in Britain during the Second World War, when rationing made a rubbed-in topping a thrifty alternative to pastry. Bar versions, with a pressed shortbread base and a crumble on top, are a later idea that suits a square pan and a lunchbox.
